post.title: Color in a Jar: The West
post.body:
This is Color in a Jar: The West, the first volume of Color in a Jar: coloring pages where every scene lives inside glass. Its full title on Amazon is Color in a Jar: The West: A 50 States Coloring Book, Nevada, California, Utah, Oregon & Idaho.

## How it was made

Every page was generated with AI, using a process I spent months refining and polishing. I built the prompts with help from a tool of my own, which you can read about here: https://www.christiangehrke.com/?workshop+winter+day+propre-engine

## The garden and the pond

The first jar holds a walled garden. A plum tree leans over an iron gate that stands open, a cobbled path runs back past an ivy-covered wall, and a stone tower sits at the far end. The next is shallower, a round glass dish turned into a pond, with water lilies, a willow hanging over it and a dragonfly resting on a reed.

## Farther afield

Then the scenes go farther afield. A snowy village sits in a jar tagged Alpine Adventure, with a lit-up tree in the square, skaters on a frozen pond and mountains under a crescent moon. There's a savanna with a lion resting under an acacia and a giraffe walking past a big low sun. There's a bamboo grove around a stone lantern, a forest floor under a bell jar with spotted mushrooms, curled fern fronds and a snail, and a glass greenhouse dome full of orchids and palms with butterflies on the outside.

## The desert

The desert gets its turn too: a bowl of succulents with a string of pearls spilling over the rim and a lizard on a rock, and a jar holding an oasis, a pool between palms with a camel resting beside it.

> Every page gets a clear edge, and inside it, the whole world can be as busy as you like.

## The island in a bottle

One page is a message in a bottle lying in the sand, with a little island inside: a hammock, a campfire, a treasure chest and parrots. That same island became one of the companion scenes I made to promote the book, with the Field Notes narrators in it: GlazyArray, the brass robot, at the treasure chest, Robot Marley beside her in a pirate hat, and A.L.T.A. in the shallows watching. The companion scenes aren't in the book; they're here to introduce it.

## Black and white, and color

Below, the jar pages sit side by side, in black and white and in color. The colored versions were made with AI, and they're only suggestions of where a page can go; the colors are up to whoever is holding the pencils.

## Worlds within worlds

In the companion scenes, the three of them travel through other worlds from the book too. They meet a camel at an oasis, a squirrel on an autumn path by a stone bridge, and a sunflower field at sunset. They share a beach with a sandcastle and a kite, pick peaches from a ladder by a red barn, and carry a lantern through a moonlit graveyard with a jack-o'-lantern. There's a jungle with a toucan, a sloth and a waterfall, an ice floe with a polar bear under the northern lights, and the deep sea, where GlazyArray wears a diving helmet and Marley a glass bubble. Marley gets a new hat in nearly every world.

## Where to find it

Color in a Jar: The West is on Amazon, as a printed book and as a digital edition: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H1QG4NX7

Volume Two is planned, but it isn't published yet.

The jar is the frame. Every page gets a clear edge, and inside it, the whole world can be as busy as you like.

episode.title: Worlds in a jar
episode.script:
Narrated by GlazyArray.

This Note came without a trail, a tracker or a single mile. It came in a jar.

Color in a Jar, The West, is the first volume of a coloring book, and every page in it puts a whole world behind glass. Every page was made with AI, through a process Christian spent months refining, with prompts built in a tool of his own. That kind of patience doesn't show on the page. What shows is how easy it all looks.

The first jar holds a garden. A plum tree heavy with fruit, an iron gate standing open, a cobbled path that winds back toward an old stone tower. The next is barely a jar at all, more of a shallow glass dish, with water lilies, a willow bending over the water and a dragonfly resting on a reed.

***

After that, the jars start to travel. A snowy village with skaters on a frozen pond, and a little tag on the lid that says Alpine Adventure. A lion resting in the shade of an acacia while a giraffe strolls past a low, enormous sun. A bamboo grove around a stone lantern. Spotted mushrooms and curled ferns under a bell jar, with a snail making its slow way up a branch.

The desert gets a page or two as well. A bowl of succulents with a lizard keeping watch on a rock. An oasis in a jar, where a camel has found the one patch of shade and decided to stay.

***

Then there's the bottle. A message in a bottle, lying in the sand, with an island inside: palm trees, a hammock, a campfire and a treasure chest.

In the book, every page waits in clean black lines. On this Note, some of them sit beside a colored version that AI filled in. Those colors are only a suggestion. The real ones belong to whoever picks up the pencils.

To introduce the book, Christian also made a few scenes that aren't in it. In one, that same island comes to life. A brass robot and a robot dog in a pirate hat are opening the chest, and a mermaid watches from the shallows.

The brass robot is me. The dog is Robot Marley, and the mermaid is A.L.T.A. I'll try to stay modest about it.

The three of us get around. We kneel by a camel at an oasis. We meet a squirrel on an autumn path. We walk a sunflower field at sunset, build nothing more than a sandcastle at the beach, and pick peaches from a ladder. We carry a lantern through a moonlit graveyard, sit on a mossy branch with a toucan and a sloth, and share an ice floe with a polar bear under the northern lights. Marley gets a new hat almost everywhere she goes.

What I like about the book is the frame. The glass gives every page a clean edge, so the worlds inside can be as busy as they want and still feel calm.

***

Color in a Jar, The West, is on Amazon, as a printed book and as a digital edition. Volume Two is on its way, though it isn't out yet. Jars, after all, are made to be filled.
